title: Keyless completion attempt identity drifts with the work basis it completes
outcome: An unlinked keyless completion retry is recognised by an identity that does not change as a side effect of the completion it is retrying, so recovery returns the prior result because the intent matches rather than because a fallback branch caught a key that had already moved
acceptance: Repeated intent after a reopen or a new run is decided deliberately and stated, rather than inherited from whatever the key happens to hash

The attempt identity for an unlinked keyless completion is derived from inputs the retry can reproduce, and a source trace shows it no longer changes merely because completion advanced the work revision, lifecycle or claim
The pre-existing completed-work recovery branches remain, but a test shows the recovered result is reached by matching identity rather than only by the fallback

completion.summary: Delivered and validated stable same-run completion retry identity with safe reclaim and authority guidance; required corrections sealed and authoritative review pair accepted.
